title: Market structure *complete*
yt_title: Market Structure Fully Explained – HH/HL, BOS, CHoCH & Multi-Timeframe (H4 → M5) on Gold

segs.say: If you don't know which way the market is moving, every entry is a coin flip. That's why market structure is the foundation of everything we do on the gold chart.

In this video we'll go through it completely: highs and lows in a trend, the break of structure, the change of character – and how to connect several timeframes, from the four-hour to the five-minute chart.
Important up front: this is educational content, not investment advice. Trading involves risk of loss. Practise new strategies on a demo account first.

chapters.title: The *uptrend*
chapters.hook: How to read an uptrend correctly

segs.say: Let's start with the uptrend. A trend isn't an opinion – it's a sequence of highs and lows that you can clearly read on the chart.
The market rises and forms a high. If it's exceeded later, we call it a higher high, or H H.
Then comes a pullback. What matters is where it ends: if the new low stays above the previous one, it's a higher low, or H L.
Now you mark the last high. This line shows you where the trend has to prove it's continuing.
If a candle closes above this line, we have a break of structure to the upside. The trend is confirmed.
And it continues like this: a new higher low, a new break of structure. As long as this chain holds, you only look for trade ideas on the buy side.
The downtrend works exactly the other way round. Here you look for lower lows and lower highs.
The market falls and forms a low. If it's undercut, it's a lower low, or L L.
The recovery afterwards stays below the previous high. That's a lower high, or L H. The buyers no longer manage to make new highs.
The last low is now the line you watch.
If a candle closes below it, that's a break of structure to the downside. The downtrend continues.
Here too the pattern repeats. As long as lower highs and lower lows form, only sells are an option for you.
Now comes a point where many traders fail: the question of when a high is really broken.
We have an uptrend with a clear high.
After the pullback a higher low forms. The line at the last high is drawn.
Then a wick pokes above the high – but the candle closes back below it. Anyone who buys here often walks straight into a trap.
Price falls back. That wasn't a break of structure – more of a grab for the liquidity above the high.
Only this candle closes clearly above the high. Now the break of structure is confirmed.
The rule is simple: the closing price counts, not the wick. That protects you from many premature entries.
So remember:
A wick above the high doesn't count as a break.
Only the candle close confirms it.

chapters.title: Change of *Character*
chapters.hook: How to spot a trend reversal early

segs.say: No trend runs forever. The change of character is the first hint that the structure is turning.
Here we see a downtrend with lower highs and lower lows.
You mark the last lower high. It's the line the sellers have to defend.
The market makes one more lower low, but the sell-off is losing strength.
Then a candle closes above the last lower high. That's the change of character. The downtrend is broken – but the new trend isn't confirmed yet.
The reversal is only confirmed by a higher low and a break of structure to the upside. In short: the CHoCH warns, the BOS confirms.

chapters.title: From *H4* to *M5*
chapters.hook: H4 for direction, M5 for the entry

segs.say: Finally, we connect the timeframes. The bigger chart sets the direction, the smaller one gives you the precise entry.
On the four-hour chart there's an uptrend, and price is coming into a zone it previously rallied from. On the five-minute chart we still see a correction to the downside.
In the zone, a wick takes the stops below the last low. That's a sweep.
Then the five-minute chart closes above the last lower high. The change of character shows: the small structure is turning in the direction of the big trend.
The entry comes on the pullback, with the stop below the sweep low. That keeps the risk small and clearly defined.
If the plan works out, price runs toward the next high. But even the best setup can fail – that's why the stop always belongs in the trade.
Let's sum up.
Higher highs and higher lows mean an uptrend, lower highs and lower lows mean a downtrend.
A break of structure confirms the trend – but only with a candle close, not with a wick.
segs.bullet: BOS only with a candle close

segs.say: The change of character is a warning. The reversal is only confirmed with a higher low and a new break of structure.
The direction comes from the four-hour chart, the entry from the five-minute chart.
And no matter how clear the structure looks: risk only a small part of your account per trade, about one to two percent.
